FL is one area that I am really struggling with. So I think I should post some homework here and hopefully I can get some feedbacks on how to overcome my struggle. I am trying to find a set of rules that allow me to draw FLs in a mechanical way, the two rules that I have learned from RTM with regards to the creation of FL is: (1) FL is created after the break/engulf of a key SR level or another FL (2) FL is only confirmed after price has hit a target in the direction of the break/engulf.

I must admit that these two rules are giving me a lot of problems, let me

I don't quit

illustrate with this chart, it's AUDUSD from FXTOP, if I am going to draw FL, following the above two rules, then I will immediately face a problem, because where is the target?

So I wanted to draw FL#1, as it broke previous swing low at A; and I wanted to draw FL#2 as it broke swing low B. But in both cases, I am constrained by Rule (2), I need to wait for price to hit a target, the problem is, in this chart, there is no LFL that can serve as a TG, so how do I proceed?

The other thing is the definition of 'target', I have read in many places, that an FL can only be drawn after price has hit an opposing FL. This seemed to imply that only an opposing FL can be used as a target? But we don't always have opposing FL as illustrate in this example. So I think we need to make an additional rule, and that is: ALL TIME HIGH or ALL TIME LOW are automatically considered targets. Otherwise, as in the example of AUDUSD, we could wait forever to validate FL#1 and FL#2?

Thank you so much for reading this. AK

It is rare to find ourselves in a trading scenario where there isn't history to the left. We cannot apply a FL target rule in such a scenario. Thinking about handling all time lows / highs isn't the right approach.

I think you would be better served posting a couple of charts marked where you are unsure and we can help correct or confirm until it become clearer to you.

Trying to draw FL, following the basic rule: An FL is created after engulfing an opposing FL.

I don't quit

Here's the chain reaction: FL-3 engulfed FL-1 FL-4 engulfed FL-2 FL-5 engulfed FL-4 FL-6 engulfed FL-3 FL-7 engulfed FL-6 FL-8 engulfed FL-7 FL-9 engulfed FL-8 FL-10 engulfed FL-9 FL-11 engulfed FL-10 but FL-11 is not valid yet, because it hit FL-5 immediately upon engulfing FL-10, so our rules say it needs to hit the next FL of the same time scale for it to be valid.

The little DP (light blue rectangle) was the decision to engulf FL-10. It held price.

Now, on a second thought, I drew an orange rectangle from the Right Shoulder, it's a DP, and price is reacting to it at the moment. Is hitting a DP considered target reached? At the moment, my limited brain is telling me that the answer has to be YES, I would challenge anyone who can explain a chart using FL alone (no DP, no CAP), just FL, with FL being defined as the kink AFTER engulfing another FL.

At the end of the day, we go through the ordeal of drawing these FL, with one objective, trying to figure out a good location to enter a trade.

I am tempted to enter a short at the MPL of FL-B, but then... isn't that a little too obvious for every SD trader to see? Probably a better place to enter is a little higher, at FL-A above?

Any comments are very much appreciated! Merci Messieurs! AK
